paper.title: BubbleRank: Safe Online Learning to Re-Rank via Implicit Click Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning to re-rank in a stochastic click bandit (D = [K])
unmapped: Clicks observed at every position are products of an unobserved examination indicator and an attraction indicator (stochastic click bandit; covers cascade and position-based models)

Assumption 1 (A1-A5) on examination probabilities: optimal list is descending attraction order, examination depends only on set of higher-ranked items, decreasing examination, examination scaling, lowest examination in optimal list
Number of items L equals number of positions K (re-ranking)
Learner is given an initial base list R_0 (warm start); regret depends on its number of incorrectly-ordered pairs |V_0|
Safety: displayed lists have at most |V_0| + K/2 incorrectly ordered pairs
settings.definition_quote: An instance of a \emph{stochastic click bandit} \cite{batchrank} is a tuple $(K, L, P_\alpha, P_\chi)$ ... We follow the setting in \cref{sec:stochastic click bandit}, except that $\cD = [K]$.

symbols.V_0: number of incorrectly-ordered item pairs in the initial base list R_0

conditions: Delta_min = min_k alpha(k) - alpha(k+1) (gap between consecutive attraction probabilities)
tuning: delta in (0,1) is the confidence parameter of BubbleRank

source.label: thm:upper bound
source.quote: In any stochastic click bandit that satisfies \cref{sec:assumptions}, and for any $\delta \in (0, 1)$, the expected $n$-step regret of $\bubblerank$ is bounded as R(n) \leq 180 K \frac{\chi_{\max}}{\chi_{\min}} \frac{K - 1 + 2 \abs{\cV_0}}{\Delta_{\min}} \log(1 / \delta) + \delta^\frac{1}{2} K^3 n^2.

results.notes: Regret defined through expected rewards, so pseudo-regret. Bound holds for any n given delta; to obtain O(log n / Delta_min) the paper sets delta = n^{-4}, which requires knowing n (doubling trick suggested otherwise). Proof of Lemma 7 uses delta <= 1/e. Delta_min here is gap between consecutive items' attraction probabilities.

symbols.V_0: number of incorrectly-ordered item pairs in the initial base list R_0

conditions: holds uniformly over t with probability at least 1 - delta^(1/2) K^2 n

source.label: lem:safety
source.quote: Let $\cV_0 = \cV(\cR_0)$ be the incorrectly-ordered item pairs in the initial base list $\cR_0$. Then the number of incorrectly-ordered item pairs in any displayed list $\rnd{\cR}_t$ is at most $\abs{\cV_0} + K / 2$, that is $\abs{\cV(\rnd{\cR}_t)} \leq \abs{\cV_0} + K / 2$ holds uniformly over time with probability of at least $1 - \delta^\frac{1}{2} K^2 n$.

results.notes: Safety guarantee (number of incorrectly ordered pairs in displayed lists), not a regret bound.
